report:
Your position is well-supported by high-quality medical research: **there is currently no clear evidence that hypnosis helps people quit smoking.**

While hypnotherapy is frequently promoted for smoking cessation, rigorous clinical evaluations do not demonstrate its effectiveness over standard alternatives:

* **Cochrane Systematic Review:** A comprehensive Cochrane Review evaluating randomized controlled trials concluded that there is insufficient evidence to show hypnotherapy is more effective for long-term smoking cessation than unassisted quitting or other forms of behavioral support. If any benefit exists, current evidence suggests it is minimal at best (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD001008_does-hypnotherapy-help-people-who-are-trying-stop-smoking).
* **National Institutes of Health (NCCIH):** The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health states that studies evaluating hypnosis for quitting smoking have produced conflicting results, and there is insufficient evidence to show it is superior to quitting on your own or using standard support (https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/quitting-smoking, https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/hypnosis).

### Conclusion
Scientific consensus does not support hypnotherapy as a reliable or effective intervention for smoking cessation. Major medical guidelines instead recommend evidence-based treatments with proven efficacy, such as cognitive-behavioral counseling, nicotine replacement therapy (NRT), or approved prescription medications.
